title: CHAPTER 8: HISTORY OF ODISHA – ANCIENT PERIOD

blocks.content: Evidence of Stone Age habitation has been found at Kuliana (Mayurbhanj), Baripada, and Ushakothi. Chalcolithic settlements are known from the Mahanadi and Brahmani valleys. The ancient name of Odisha was 'Kalinga', and it was also known as 'Udra', 'Kongoda', and 'Tosali'.

Kalinga was a powerful ancient kingdom in the region of present-day Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh. It had a strong navy and maritime trade. The Battle of Kalinga (261 BCE) was a turning point in Indian history.

cells: 261 BCE – Ashoka (Maurya) conquered Kalinga; ~1,00,000 killed; Ashoka renounced war and embraced Buddhism
1st century BCE; greatest Kalinga ruler; expanded empire; built Hathigumpha caves
Cave inscription of King Kharavela at Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves near Bhubaneswar; Brahmi script
Kalinga had flourishing trade with South-East Asia; sailors called 'Sadhabas'
Annual festival at Cuttack celebrating ancient maritime trade with Bali, Java, Sumatra

blocks.content: The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves near Bhubaneswar are rock-cut caves from the 1st century BCE, associated with Jainism and King Kharavela. Hathigumpha (Elephant Cave) bears the longest Brahmi inscription of King Kharavela. Ranigumpha is the most elaborately decorated cave with two-storied structure.

After the decline of the Kalinga kingdom, the region was influenced by the Gupta Empire, Somavamshis (6th–11th century), and later the Gangas. The Somavamshis had their capital at Sonepur/Suvarnapur (now Subarnapur). The Eastern Gangas ruled from Kalinganagara (Mukhalingam) and later Cuttack.

The Eastern Ganga dynasty (11th–15th century) was the most powerful dynasty in medieval Odisha. They were great temple builders. Anantavarman Chodaganga built the Jagannath Temple at Puri (12th century). Narasimhadeva I built the Sun Temple at Konark (1250 CE).
